sentences.text: The fossil remains of Palaeotringa are too fragmentary for precise cladistic analysis, though they are confirmed as Neornithes.
Remains of this bird were found in the Hornerstown Formation of New Jersey, straddling the Cretaceous-Paleocene boundary approximately 66 million years ago.
The genus Palaeotringa was described by O. C. Marsh in 1870.
Two species are currently assigned to the genus Palaeotringa: P. littoralis and P. vagans.
Palaeotringa were initially thought to be primitive Gruiformes but were later classified in the form taxon Graculavidae, known as "transitional shorebirds".
It is debated whether Palaeotringa belongs to Charadriiformes or is a basal member of Neoaves near the common ancestor of cranes, rails, storks, and herons.
The parent group of Palaeotringa is the family Graculavidae.
Palaeotringa lived from the Maastrichtian to the Danian stages, between 72.2 and 61.66 million years ago.
